topic: Outship (outship.ai): verified capabilities for a 60-second 'Hire AI-native engineers' promo

claims.claim: Outship is a live recruiting platform (YC Winter 2025, status Active) that 'records and analyzes how engineering candidates use coding agents.' Homepage title/tagline: 'Hire amazing engineers by seeing how they use AI'; hero headline: 'Hire AI Native Engineers'.

sources.title: Outship: Hire amazing engineers by seeing how they use AI

claims.notes: Founders Saner Cakir (CEO) and Kayla Lee (COO). Site live with app login at app.outship.ai. Small team (~3 per third-party profile).

claims.claim: Hero copy: 'See who's engineering and who's vibe coding. Candidates work with real coding agents like Claude Code and Codex, and you see every decision they make.'
claims.notes: Matches storyline line 'See who's engineering, and who's just vibe-coding' almost verbatim. Site writes 'vibe coding' (no hyphen).

claims.claim: Problem framing on the site: 'Engineers are shipping with AI everyday' / 'It's time for hiring processes to stop pretending otherwise' / 'Traditional technical interviews were designed for a different era'.
claims.notes: Storyline opening lines are paraphrases of these headings.

claims.claim: Realistic project tasks: 'Outship supports virtually any task. Each candidate gets a real VM with VS Code, dependencies, and AI agents configured.' and 'Import interview projects you already use from GitHub, ask candidates to solve a past bug, or even have them ship a real PR to your product.' CTA: 'Create your first task'.
claims.notes: Tasks are repo-based (imported from GitHub), not a free-text 'project brief' generator. Supports 'Real tasks from your own codebase'.

claims.claim: Candidates use real coding agents: 'Real coding agents like Claude Code and Codex'. FAQ: 'You can provide access through the Anthropic or OpenAI APIs, or through cloud providers like AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, and Azure. Your keys are proxied so candidates never see them. You can also have candidates log in and authenticate with their own accounts.'
claims.notes: Named agents are Claude Code (Anthropic) and Codex (OpenAI), not 'ChatGPT'. Site also loads Cursor and Qwen logo assets but the copy only names Claude Code and Codex.

claims.claim: Real IDE/terminal: 'Candidates code on a real Linux VM, so virtually any language or framework works. We also support live dev servers'. 'Remote VM by default. Local mode is also available if you want candidates to use their own setup, including MCPs, CLIs, and custom skills.'
claims.notes: Homepage demo shows VS Code-style explorer plus Claude Code / Codex / bash terminal tabs.

claims.claim: Recruiters see everything: 'Outship captures everything a candidate does while building: every prompt, every edit, every command, every decision.' 'It's like watching every candidate think out loud. You see how they decompose the problem, drive the agent, and recover when things break.' Demo UI: 'Scrub to explore the session'.

sources.title: Outship homepage (The Process Is the Signal)

claims.notes: Supports 'deliverable, code, how they use agents'. Meta description: 'capture and analyze that process alongside the final code' (YC page).

claims.claim: Automated analysis against a rubric: 'Every prompt, every edit, every command, and every decision is analyzed to show you who's engineering and who's vibe coding'; demo shows 'Analyzing session against rubric…' with categories Codebase Orientation, Architectural Research, Full-Stack Execution, Agent Communication, Verification & Shipping, contrasting 'Experienced engineer' vs 'Inexperienced vibe coder'.

sources.title: Outship homepage (See exactly how candidates work)

claims.notes: Site does not explicitly say 'AI agents score candidates' nor show numeric scores; it says sessions are 'analyzed' against a rubric and produces 'reports' (FAQ: 'sample interview and the corresponding reports'). Rubric category names differ from the storyline's 8 dimensions.

claims.claim: Sending to candidates: 'Import a task repo from GitHub and send an invite link for a take home or an interview. We spin up a cloud workspace for them to work in.' ATS: 'Outship integrates with common ATS providers like Ashby, Greenhouse, and Workday. We also support automated flows, for example routing every candidate that applies through a specific channel into a task.'
claims.notes: No 'hundreds of candidates' figure on the site; scale is implied via invite links and ATS automated routing.

claims.claim: Outcome stats on site: 'Top 1% Standout engineers your competitors miss'; '2-3 hours Of your engineers' time saved per candidate'.
Availability: no public pricing; sales-led via 'Book a Demo'. FAQ: 'Most of our customers are ready to send their first assessment the same day they onboard.'

open_questions: Does Outship produce numeric candidate scores/rankings, or qualitative rubric reports only? Site shows rubric analysis but no score.
Is the analysis performed by AI agents? Site says sessions are 'analyzed' but does not name the analyzer.

Can customers define custom rubric dimensions (e.g., the storyline's 8: code quality, problem decomposition, adaptability, testing approach, tech stack decisions, iterative mindset, verifies AI output, debugging instinct)?
Throughput limits: any stated cap or support for sending to 'hundreds' of candidates at once?
Is there a free task-creation flow from a written project brief, or only GitHub repo import?
Official press kit / brand guidelines: none found; logo wordmark was rebuilt from the site's header (mark SVG path + 'outship' set in the site's own Saans Medium font).
